name: Context Kit Instrument
author: KyaniteLabs
description: Serves the canonical context-kit (KyaniteLabs, MIT) — measured context engineering for local LLM agent harnesses — as a local http-json service. The kit's runnable modules execute for real in-process: reasoning-style routing and byte-stable prepends (style steering), sandboxed symbol-level reads accelerated by the kit's own mtime-validated cache, projection-time dedup/compaction, and progressive disclosure with content-addressed spills. The kit's measurement instruments need a live llama.cpp-class endpoint and are pinned not-runnable headless, never faked. Companion notes: simongonzalezdc/resonant-context-notes.

tools.name: contextkit.status
tools.description: Report service version, vendored kit identity (name, version, license, upstream commit, vendored file count), served modules, cache and spill counters, and the honesty note: the measurement instruments are not runnable headless by this service.

tools.name: contextkit.styles
tools.description: The vendored kit's three reasoning-style prompts (fused, caveman, ponytail) verbatim, plus the three style laws and the regime condition from the kit's README (style steering is effective where the model would overthink; route per session, not per turn).

tools.name: contextkit.style.route
tools.description: Run the vendored style_layer() router: which style (if any) applies to this turn. Auto dials fused everywhere except the creative lane and instant turns; returns null for no-style turns. Style steers verbosity; it is never a budget cap.

text.description: The turn's user text the router inspects.

think_mode.description: instant turns never get a style.

tools.name: contextkit.style.prepend
tools.description: Apply a style byte-stably with the vendored prepend_stable(): the style text LEADS the leading system message identically on every request, so the prompt cache holds. Choose the style with contextkit.style.route.

tools.name: contextkit.doc.list
tools.description: List every file in the hash-pinned vendored kit tree (README, PATTERNS.md, CREDITS.md, third-party notices, license, and the kit's Python modules); these are the only paths contextkit.doc.get accepts.

tools.name: contextkit.doc.get
tools.description: Fetch one vendored kit file verbatim (README, integration patterns, credits, notices, license, or module source) by exact manifest path. The kit's ethos is 'adapt, don't install' — read the module before adapting it.

tools.name: contextkit.munch.read_symbol
tools.description: Symbol-level read with the vendored read_symbol(): one function/class (signature, docstring line, line span, optional body) from a sandboxed sample Python file instead of a whole-file read — the kit's measured -98% tool-bytes move. Reads are confined to this add-on's var/samples; misses list candidate symbols; results flow through the kit's own mtime-validated cache.

path.description: Sandbox-relative path under var/samples; .py files only (the kit's rule).

name.description: Function or class name to read.

body.description: Include the full source body. Defaults to false.

tools.name: contextkit.diet.project
tools.description: Run the vendored projection diet verbatim (kit.diet.project): budget elision of oldest tool results, identical-output dedup to stubs, and long-session compaction — view-only passes over an event log; the input is never mutated. Identical 3x5KB repeats project to ~5.1KB (-66%, ARITHMETIC).

events.description: Event dicts; convention is {"kind": "tool_result", "content": str} plus your own fields, which pass through untouched. Max 5000 events.

min_body.description: Bodies under this are never stubbed. Defaults to 200.

tools.name: contextkit.diet.disclose
tools.description: Progressive disclosure with the vendored disclose(): texts over the limit become a head+tail preview with the full body spilled to a content-addressed file under this add-on's var/spill/ (path named in the preview, redacted). Guard read-backs yourself — if the model re-reads more than ~15% of spills, raise the limit (PATTERNS.md #6).

label.description: Label used in the preview note. Defaults to output.
